title: Toxcatl massacre at the Templo Mayor
summary: In May 1520, during the Toxcatl festival, Pedro de Alvarado and Spanish troops attacked unarmed Mexica nobles gathered in the Templo Mayor precinct of Tenochtitlan while Cortés was away on the coast. The killings set off a sustained Mexica assault, the death of Moctezuma and the Spaniards' flight from the city in the Noche Triste.

uncertainty.note: Sources agree on May 1520. Kruell gives 23 May; other accounts differ by a few days. Julian date, not converted.

as_recorded.calendar: Julian, as given by the author

where.modern_name: Templo Mayor, Historic Centre of Mexico City, Mexico
where.historical_name: Templo Mayor precinct of Mexico-Tenochtitlan, capital of the Mexica (Aztec) Triple Alliance

importance.justification: The massacre turned a tense Spanish occupation into open war, ending in the Spaniards' expulsion and the 1521 conquest campaign.

audience_note: Describes the mass killing of unarmed civilians at a religious ceremony.
